title: Justice League Receives Local Media Attention
description: The Lansing State Journal published a front page article describing JLGLM's mission, leadership, and early financial contributions from area churches.
quote: Education about reparations will continue beyond the $1 million goal.

title: First Public Presentation
description: JLGLM hosted Rev. Jimmie R. Hawkins for book discussions and signings at Socialight Society and the Downtown Capital Area District Library. These events introduced its reparations framework to the community.

title: Apology at Lansing Reachout Christian Center
description: JLGLM coordinated a public apology and reparations event at Lansing Reachout Christian Center, linking repentance with structural action and civic public witness.
quote: An apology frees and liberates both groups.

title: First Presbyterian Church of Holt Joins
description: First Presbyterian Church of Holt pledged $20,000 to support the Justice League's reparations work as an expression of faith, repentance, and hope.

title: Quaker Meeting in Lansing Joins
description: Red Cedar Friends Meeting made a $7,000 payment at the end of its fiscal year and hoped to continue annual payments.

title: Second Public Apology at the Capitol
description: Faith leaders and community members gathered on the Capitol lawn for a Juneteenth apology based on the PC(USA) litany of repentance. State Senator Sarah Anthony welcomed those gathered.
quote: This work is about repair. It is not charity, it is a moral response to a historic harm.

title: Edgewood United Church Contributes
description: Edgewood United Church committed endowment and individual resources to reparations, reporting a total payment of $173,260.

title: All Saints Episcopal Church Contributes
description: All Saints Episcopal Church in East Lansing presented $130,470.62 to JLGLM, one of the League's largest single congregational gifts.

title: Coalition Growth and Press Attention
description: Regional media described JLGLM's development into a maturing multi-church fund structure and highlighted the move from acknowledgment of harm to tangible repair.

title: Local United Nations Association Honors Ms. Bryan
description: The United Nations Association-USA Greater Lansing Chapter honored Ms. Willye Bryan as a 2023 Global Goals Local Leader, linking the model to global goals on poverty, education, inequality, and justice.
quote: My life has been shaped by segregation. That history shaped my commitment to stand in the breach and insist on repair.

title: Recognition in the Congressional Record and Second Fall Celebration
description: Representative Elissa Slotkin entered a formal commendation of JLGLM into the Congressional Record. JLGLM also held its second annual Fall Celebration at Gregory's soul food restaurant.

title: Reparations Monday and Early Recurring Commitment
description: JLGLM recognized Reparations Monday as a dedicated giving day. The Chronicle News reported more than $350,000 raised since founding, while Sycamore Creek United Methodist Church pledged 1% of its endowment annually for three years.

title: The Cost of Inheritance Film Screening and Panel
description: Nearly 100 people gathered for The Cost of Inheritance film screening and panel Q&A, featuring scholars and JLGLM leadership.

title: How Did We Get Here? Part I
description: The first annual panel at East Lansing Public Library launched a dialogue on local reparations and the racial wealth gap. The work helped establish a $350,000-plus endowment for economic justice.

title: Unity Spiritual Center of Lansing Contributes
description: Unity Spiritual Center of Lansing made a reparations contribution to the Justice League of Greater Lansing Michigan.

title: National NPR Story
description: NPR's All Things Considered featured a grassroots Michigan effort raising reparations while government action lagged.

title: Mandela Washington Fellowship Collaboration
description: JLGLM collaborated with Mandela Washington Fellowship participants at Michigan State University. Fellows produced a congratulatory video honoring inaugural scholarship recipients and helped secure a state proclamation.
quote: Working with Prince Solace and the Justice League enriched our civic engagement institute and helped secure a proclamation from Governor Whitmer.

title: First Reparations Scholarship Disbursement
description: JLGLM issued its first reparations-funded scholarships. Ten African American graduates each received $5,000 after essays, interviews, and verified enrollment. The recognition ceremony brought together students, families, clergy, and JLGLM leadership.
quote: We have made a start. We have affected this community.

title: Unitarian Universalist Church of Greater Lansing Contributes
description: UUCGL contributed through special plate collections and its Reparations Team, reporting a total reparation payment of $86,134.50.

title: Third Annual Fall Celebration
description: JLGLM held its third annual Fall Celebration at MSU Federal Credit Union headquarters, highlighting three years of fund growth, interfaith coalition building, and program delivery.
quote: Reparations are not merely financial, they are spiritual, communal acts of restoration.

title: Reparations Monday and Public Education
description: WILX reported JLGLM's year-over-year progress, including $50,000 in scholarships and the upcoming Farmland art exhibit at the Broad Art Museum.

title: Reparations in Art and Public Discourse
description: The Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum opened Farmland: Food, Justice and Sovereignty, integrating JLGLM's historical framing with contemporary visual art.
quote: This has been one of the most meaningful partnerships in my time at the MSU Broad Art Museum.

title: First Home Build: Asset-Based Reparations
description: JLGLM and the Eastside Community Action Center supported construction of a home for a senior African American first-time homebuyer on McCullough Street. ECAC provided homeowner training, savings support, and transition guidance.
quote: Home ownership is possible for individuals who sincerely desire it and work toward it.

title: Regional Juneteenth Collaboration
description: JLGLM hosted a community session at Flint's 53rd Annual Traditional Juneteenth Celebration, extending educational reach and strengthening regional reparations networks.

title: Justice League of Greater Kalamazoo Established
description: Organizers formally launched the Justice League of Greater Kalamazoo after preparatory meetings with JLGLM leadership. This became the first confirmed regional adoption of Lansing's faith-based reparations structure.
quote: This is a movement grounded in faith and accountability. Lansing can become a national model for reparative work.

title: Second Scholarship Cohort
description: JLGLM awarded a second cohort of 10 African American students reparations-funded scholarships of $2,500 each. Recipients were selected through essays, interviews, and verified enrollment.
quote: Creating a platform where students could speak about intergenerational wealth gaps was very powerful.

title: Second Home Build
description: JLGLM advanced its homeownership pillar with a second reparations-supported home on McCullough Street, adjacent to the first home, again in partnership with ECAC.

title: Fourth Anniversary Fall Celebration
description: JLGLM's Fourth Anniversary Fall Celebration at MSU Federal Credit Union offered a four-year overview of fund development, scholarships, housing, coalition growth, and strategy. University United Methodist Church announced a $100,000 multi-year pledge.

title: How Did We Get Here? Part II and Stables Communities Foundation Support
description: Part II at Delta Township District Library expanded church partnerships and grew the endowment to more than $500,000. The Stables Communities Foundation also recognized JLGLM as a grant recipient supporting advocacy, empowerment, and community strengthening.
